races.name: Jenningsbet Over 200 Shops Nationwide Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Love Alive
runners_data.note: John Butler's 3yo hold-up filly has finished third twice at 6f on good ground, but Brighton's sharp track profile rarely rewards late runners, and her 0 wins from 12 similar-going runs makes this trip a structural challenge more than a going concern.

runners_data.name: Havana Jag
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's 3yo has front-running tendencies and consistent placed form at 6f on good ground, though the presence of Mister Moet means he won't get a soft lead; Ashley Lewis claims 3lbs and the horse's seven runs without a win warrant caution at face value.

runners_data.name: Cape Toronada
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 3yo boasts a win and two placed efforts from just eight runs in similar ground conditions, and his natural prominent style is perfectly calibrated for this race shape — 44 days off the track is the main question, but William Carson's experience on this course is a meaningful positive.

runners_data.name: Mister Moet
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's 3yo carries hood headgear and has a win on the board at 5f on soft, but his record of just 1 place from 15 runs on good-type ground is a significant flag; the pace duel with Havana Jag risks costing him on both fronts, going out hard and potentially not lasting home at 6f.

runners_data.name: Beach Partee
runners_data.note: The other Dixon runner in the field, wearing a visor, has placed four times without winning and has zero placed runs from 15 similar-going starts — her prominent style keeps her in the picture, but her record suggests she consistently finds one or more too good at the business end.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Jag and Mister Moet are both confirmed front-runners in a field of just five, meaning the lead will be contested from the outset over Brighton's undulating 6f on good-to-firm ground. With two horses fighting for the same early real estate, the pace is likely to be honest rather than truly suicidal, but neither is the type to concede willingly, so there will be genuine pressure through the first two furlongs. Cape Toronada sits just off the pace in a prominent role and should be well-placed to capitalise if the lead duo soften each other, while Love Alive's hold-up style places her at a structural disadvantage on this sharp Brighton track where late ground is hard to find. This race shape — a contested lead with genuine early fractions — most favours the prominent handy profile that travels close to the pace without burning energy fighting for the front, giving Cape Toronada's style the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Jag and Mister Moet push each other through the early stages, leaving the prominent-tracking Cape Toronada ideally poised.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off the pace through the first half of the race, and the horse travelling just behind in a rhythm claims the decisive advantage entering the final two furlongs. Cape Toronada's course-distance form and proven winning ability at 6f on good ground makes this the standout profile for this race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If one lead horse (most likely Havana Jag) edges out Mister Moet early and finds a comfortable solo rhythm through the race.
scenarios.body: With the contest for the lead settled quickly, the eventual pace-setter settles into an economical gallop and simply isn't pegged back by the hold-up horses on a track that doesn't encourage late runs. Havana Jag's better recent course-and-distance profile and the use of a 3lb-claiming jockey make this the more plausible sole-leader scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Swooper
scenarios.trigger: If the front pair run each other ragged and the fractions are genuinely fast enough to open a late closing lane.
scenarios.body: A genuine burn-up between Havana Jag and Mister Moet creates a truly strong pace and the field strings out, giving a hold-up horse a rare opportunity on this track. Love Alive is the only true hold-up runner in the field, but her limited placings in similar-going conditions and lack of a win temper confidence in this scenario materialising.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fizzles, Dead Heat
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner fully commits and the race evolves into a moderately-run affair that compresses the finish.
scenarios.body: A tactical, slowly-run race shuffles the playing field as the pace advantage is neutralised and Beach Partee, who has consistently placed without winning, could find herself running on from just off the pace into a tight finish. Her visor headgear and consistent placed form give her a small chance in a muddled scenario, though her zero wins in 15 similar-going runs significantly limits expectation.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Havana Jag or Mister Moet gets to the lead uncontested in the first furlong — if one jumps out cleanly and the other fails to match strides early, the dynamic shifts from contested to solo-led and Cape Toronada's chance narrows slightly.

Cape Toronada returns after 44 days off the track; monitor early market moves and paddock demeanour — a fresh horse that travels keenly could be a positive or a negative depending on how Tony Carroll has had him tuned up.

Mister Moet's hood headgear is notable — if it fails to settle him in a pace duel, he risks burning out before the final furlong and becoming a non-factor in the finish despite his higher early position.

Love Alive has run at 6f on good ground just once (third at Yarmouth), so this is a marginal step up in trip on a track that doesn't suit hold-up horses — watch how early Alistair Rawlinson commits to get her competitive, as any delay will likely leave her with too much to do.

Beach Partee's consistent placed efforts mask a horse who has never won — if the pace is genuinely contested, watch whether Tyler Heard drops her back slightly to find a clear run, as her visor suggests connections are trying to sharpen her focus into a finish.

races.name: Jenningsbet In Deal Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Aspire To Glory
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race and almost certainly goes straight to the lead; Tony Carroll-trained connections send her out with blinkers/tongue-tie, and her OR=48 makes her competitive at the top of this classified band, though she is racing at a slightly unusual style-fit for her recent record with no sim-going wins from 15 attempts.

runners_data.name: Celebrating Ethel
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll has 3/32 runners placed over the past fortnight and the gelding has a win on similar going, but she is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural role has been pushed forward on the map simply because the rear is oversubscribed — her chance depends on whether the tempo is fast enough to suit a finisher who needs horses to come back to her.

runners_data.name: First Encounter
runners_data.note: Tactically prominent and eyecatching in headgear, but only one run from 15 on similar going ending in a place, and John Gallagher's yard is 0/7 in the last 14 days; will try to press the leader but the Brighton climb may expose her limited recent form.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Sign
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes the ride on an eight-year-old who has shown genuine placed form on Good ground over this trip, recording three placed efforts in seven similar-going starts; a natural pressing type who could benefit if Aspire To Glory's lead is reeled in on the climb.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a genuine hold-up style and two similar-going runs under his belt; Molly Gunn's 5lb claim is an asset in a tight race, though his recent record of 860685 suggests consistency issues, and a slow pace makes him an each-way rather than win proposition.

runners_data.name: Rock Master
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with seven sim-going runs and three placed efforts, but carries a clear style-fit discount: his natural style sees him come from the rear and the redistributed mapping into midfield reflects how crowded this race's hold-up sector is; Cieren Fallon's experience is a plus but the tempo is unlikely to suit.

runners_data.name: Rovinia
runners_data.note: The standout form profile in the field with four placed efforts from five recent similar-going starts; a natural hold-up runner who has managed to place twice over this exact trip on Good ground, and Roger Teal's patient placing could pay off if she can sit closer than usual in a compressed field.

runners_data.name: Sangara
runners_data.note: 305 days off the track is a serious concern and the warning flag for fading in finishes makes her risky at any price; three of her nine sim-going runs have yielded placed finishes but the combination of layoff and finishing tendency reduces confidence sharply.

runners_data.name: Skyolaire
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who carries a weight allowance of 128lbs and has shown middle-distance form on Good and Firm, but is another genuine hold-up type who has been mapped into midfield by necessity rather than natural inclination; Jeff Mullins is 0/0 in the last fortnight and 45 days between runs is a mild concern.

races.paceDynamic: Aspire To Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, facing no genuine pace rival to push her along, she is highly likely to dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's turning mile. First Encounter and Rainbow Sign will press for prominent positions behind her, but neither has the natural gate speed to threaten Aspire To Glory's lead, meaning the early fractions are unlikely to be testing. The field behind is packed with hold-up horses — River Wharfe, Rovinia, Sangara, and three redistributed closers in Rock Master, Skyolaire, and Celebrating Ethel — but with only one horse setting a gentle, controlled tempo, those held up at the rear face a stiff ask to generate the momentum needed to reel in the leader. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can sit closer to the pace than their natural style dictates and produce a sustained finish in the final two furlongs, rather than pure closers who need a strong gallop to close ground. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Aspire To Glory is most likely to lead comfortably, with River Wharfe and Rovinia best positioned to occupy the genuinely closer berths behind the front rank.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Aspire To Glory Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Aspire To Glory bowls along uncontested and sets a steady but controlled tempo that denies closers a true target.
scenarios.body: Aspire To Glory dictates from the front without pressure, slowing the race to a crawl before quickening from two furlongs out, rewarding anything that tracked closely enough to challenge at the death; River Wharfe and Rovinia, natural hold-up runners who can sit nearer than usual in a field of redistributed closers, are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine pace is slow enough to bunch the field but Aspire To Glory ties up inside the final furlong on the testing Brighton climb.
scenarios.body: A false-paced race collapses late on the rise to the line and the finishers who have been creeping through from the back third — Rovinia and River Wharfe — have just enough run in them to collar a tiring leader; Rovinia's four places from five recent runs in similar going gives her the profile to deliver under this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Rainbow Sign or First Encounter tracks Aspire To Glory's comfortable lead closely and outkicks her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A slow gallop plays into the hands of horses just off the pace rather than deep closers, and Rainbow Sign — who has shown placed form on Good ground over this trip — has the tactical speed to sit second or third and pounce before the hold-up horses get organised.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest enough to compress the field and one of the true hold-up horses mapped to midfield finds clear running to produce a finishing burst.
scenarios.body: Rock Master, Skyolaire, or Celebrating Ethel would need to overcome their displaced position and a tempo unlikely to suit deep closers, making this a low-probability outcome; Celebrating Ethel's single course win and Rock Master's youth are marginal positives in this context.

watchPoints.text: Rovinia's four placed efforts from five recent similar-going runs make her the most consistent finisher in the field — watch whether Owen Lewis gives her a closer position than her natural style to capitalise on the slow pace.

Aspire To Glory's lack of sim-going wins (0W0P from 15 attempts) is a red flag despite her clear role as sole front-runner — if she fails to see out the mile on the Brighton climb, the race blows wide open.

Rainbow Sign with Pat Cosgrave could steal the race by tracking Aspire To Glory at close range throughout; if Cosgrave gets a soft lead and dictates a slow fractions-dominated race, the outsiders at the back have no chance.

Sangara's 305-day layoff combined with the finishing-fade flag means she should be treated with caution even if she appears well-handicapped on paper — monitor her in the paddock for condition signs before drawing conclusions.

Tony Carroll runs three horses in this race (Celebrating Ethel, River Wharfe, Rock Master) — with multiple interests, jockey deployment and potential team tactics are worth tracking in the early stages to understand stable intentions.

races.name: Sapporo Japanese Premium Lager Brighton Mile Challenge Handicap Stakes (For The Brighton Mile Challenge Trophy)

runners_data.name: Silca Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins at this exact trip and going band; Eve Johnson Houghton sends it out 18 days fresh and in form (4-1-4-1 recently), headgear unchanged — the horse to beat if it travels cleanly to the front from the off, though its STYLE_FIT flag is moot when it is genuinely the race's pace-maker.

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon is a significant booking for James Owen's four-year-old, who has placed nine times in 15 starts on similar going and won over a mile in Good ground — versatile enough to race prominently or just off the pace, and the form string 3-4-1-7-2-2 reads consistently.

runners_data.name: Newfangled
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's five-year-old has two wins and seven places from 15 comparable-going starts, and Rob Hornby gives it every chance of forcing a forward position — but this is a field thick with prominent types and it genuinely may not get the berth it needs, which tempers confidence despite a decent recent form string.

runners_data.name: Here I Bow
runners_data.note: Returning from 86 days off for Jonny Peate and Oli Rix (1 win from 7 in the last 14 days), the hold-up style is a structural disadvantage on a track where the finish comes quickly — three successive mid-field finishes in Good ground over this trip underline the concern.

runners_data.name: Tex
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave's mount has placed six times from 13 starts on similar going including wins over 7f, but the step back up to a mile after a ninth over 6f last time is speculative; the hold-up style means it needs pace that this race probably won't supply.

runners_data.name: Northern Empire
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old won impressively over 7f on Standard but has struggled to replicate that in Good ground at this distance (8th, 5th); Ashley Lewis takes a 3lb claim off which helps, yet consistent inability to fire at a mile on turf is a concern.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old is unbeaten in Good ground at this trip in a small sample (4 runs, 4/4 sim-going) and has placed over both 7f and 8f in identical conditions — Jack Callan rides and the hold-up/prominent blend suits tracking the leader from a close second position.

runners_data.name: Play Me
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's four-year-old is a natural front-runner with two wins and six places from 15 comparable-going starts, but in a field this prominent-heavy, Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) is likely to find the horse outpaced for position early and unable to settle where it races best.

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Harry Davies on Ian Williams's six-year-old veteran; three places from 15 similar-going starts and last seen running well from the rear at this trip — a hold-up horse that needs a stronger pace than this race shape is likely to generate to close the gap on handy horses at Brighton.

races.paceDynamic: Silca Bay is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing or able to push for the lead at Brighton's mile, Oliver Carmichael is almost certain to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good to Firm ground. Sea Suite and Northern Empire will press for prominent positions just behind, creating a compact early gallop rather than a searching one, which means the race is unlikely to truly test stamina — the premium will be on tactical speed and the ability to quicken from a handy position rather than grinding out a finish. This shape heavily favours horses racing prominently or in a close-up midfield berth who can respond to a decisive move in the final two furlongs; true hold-up horses like Here I Bow, Tex, and Giant face the classic Brighton dilemma of being too far back when the leaders kick. Newfangled and Play Me are both natural prominent racers who cannot all get that position in a field this packed with similar types — of the pair, Newfangled's higher-class profile and Rob Hornby's experience give it the better chance of forcing its way up, while Play Me is more likely to find itself shuffled back against its will.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Silca Bay Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Silca Bay leads unchallenged and the pace is steady enough to sustain a front-running win on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: Carmichael sets a comfortable tempo from stall one, the field strings out behind Sea Suite and Northern Empire without any surge to close the gap, and Silca Bay's finishing kick — demonstrated by two wins at this trip in similar going — proves just enough to hold on. Brighton's undulating mile suits a horse that travels smoothly from the front, and Silca Bay's OR-81 profile gives it a class edge over the hold-up horses trying to reel it in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Suite or Glen Nevis track Silca Bay closely and find a decisive turn of foot in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sea Suite has strong recent form at this trip in Good going with four placings in similar conditions, and Cieren Fallon is well-equipped to time a challenge from just off the pace. Glen Nevis showed good speed when second at this trip and distance on identical going and can pick off a tiring leader if the early gallop has been even slightly more taxing than it appeared.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace lifts enough in the middle portion to string the field out and create a genuine gap for closers to fill.
scenarios.body: Tex or Giant would need an untypically strong tempo to close the distance on a well-placed leader at Brighton, where the track's topology actively punishes horses that are detached at halfway. If the pace does lift — perhaps triggered by Northern Empire pressing from the outside — Tex's good-ground speed figures and Giant's strong recent place record at the trip give them each an outside chance of finishing fastest of all.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Positions
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent-heavy field jostles aggressively for position early and disrupts Silca Bay's clean break, causing a muddled tempo.
scenarios.body: With Newfangled and Play Me both natural front-runners pushed into midfield roles they don't want, any squeeze or stumble in the opening furlong could force a reshuffle that unsettles Silca Bay's rhythm and compresses the field into a tight bunch. In that scenario the horse with the highest raw ability and strongest finishing speed — Sea Suite with Fallon aboard — is best placed to exploit the resulting messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Silca Bay breaks cleanly — if Oliver Carmichael gets a clean break from the stall and immediately establishes a lead of even a length, the race shape locks in immediately and challenges become structurally harder at Brighton's undulating mile.

Newfangled and Play Me both want to race prominently but cannot both do so — watch the early furlongs for pushing and shoving between Rob Hornby and Donagh Murphy that could unsettle Sea Suite or Northern Empire racing just behind.

Here I Bow returns from 86 days off and Jonny Peate will need to find the right early position quickly — if the horse is flat or sluggish off that layoff it will have no chance from a hold-up berth at Brighton.

Glen Nevis's Going record is a small but clean sample — 4 from 4 in Good ground at this distance — and Jack Callan may opt to ride closer to the pace than his style tag suggests, which would make it a genuine each-way threat if Silca Bay does not kick clear.

The official going for the 3:30 is recorded as Good To Firm despite the race card listing Good — conditions are fast enough that any horse with a going concern flag on firm ground should be monitored in the pre-race going update.

races.name: Monty Bennetts 18th Birthday Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Annexation
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up specialist with Tony Carroll, showing respectable recent form over 10f on Good but mapped to midfield here as one of three true hold-up types who cannot all get their natural rear position; Cieren Fallon's booking is a positive, though racing out of role tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: It's Life
runners_data.note: Trainer Kathy Turner has a red-hot 3/4 strike rate in the last 14 days and this four-year-old bounced back to win 11 days ago over 8f on Good; at heart a hold-up runner displaced into a midfield slot by the crowded rear of this field, so finishing position could be compromised, but recent form and stable momentum are compelling angles.

runners_data.name: West Hill Rosie
runners_data.note: Bears a recorded tendency to fade in the finish which is a significant concern on Brighton's uphill straight, compounded by 45 days off and modest stamina form at this sort of trip; a true hold-up horse absorbed into midfield by the congestion at the rear, and her finishing-line weakness makes this configuration particularly awkward.

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Consistently placed on Good ground over 8f with two wins and four places from her last 12 efforts in similar conditions, and her close-tracking style suits a race where Beryl's Girl sets an uncontested pace; Edward Greatrex rode her last time out and the 14-day return with Ollie Sangster's stable firing at 7/17 is an encouraging angle.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner arrives on 25 days' rest having won over 9f on Soft and placed at similar trips on Good; Rob Hornby takes the ride and Port Darwin's best form at 9-11f suggests the 1m2f trip may be on the outer edge of comfort, but he handles Good ground and has the turn of foot to feature if the race shapes up as a late sprint.

runners_data.name: Beryl's Girl
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in this race, she sets the tactical agenda entirely; her one win came over this course-and-distance trip on Good, and racing from the front with no challenger suits, though her form figures include several disappointing efforts and a STYLE_FIT flag suggests she may not fully capitalise if others do manage to push up.

races.paceDynamic: Beryl's Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she should set a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at Brighton. The remainder of the field — Annexation, It's Life, West Hill Rosie, Buckland Belle, and Port Darwin — are all hold-up or prominent types, meaning they will be tracking Beryl's Girl at various distances rather than challenging her for the front. The field actually contains more hold-up horses than can realistically fill the rear positions; Annexation, It's Life, and West Hill Rosie are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice they will be jostling for position in a compressed group behind the leader. This race shape — one uncontested pace-setter, a bunched chasing pack — strongly favours horses with a genuine turn of foot who can quicken from a close-tracking position when the pace quickens in the final two furlongs; Buckland Belle and Port Darwin, as the least compromised hold-up types, are best placed to exploit a steady-then-sharp finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beryl's Girl Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Beryl's Girl dictates a comfortable solo lead and the hold-up pack fails to close efficiently in the straight.
scenarios.body: Beryl's Girl sets her own fractions on Good to Firm ground with no pressure, saving enough in reserve to repel any late challenge up Brighton's testing climb; the hold-up runners arrive together but find her already building a lead they cannot bridge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Quicken Past Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the bunched hold-up group carry momentum into the straight and overwhelm Beryl's Girl.
scenarios.body: A dawdle early concentrates the field and turns the final two furlongs into a sprint, neutralising any advantage Beryl's Girl holds from her lead; Buckland Belle's consistent good-ground form and recent winning run makes her the prime beneficiary of a late rush.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If Annexation or It's Life finds a clear passage from their redistributed midfield position and picks off tiring rivals.
scenarios.body: These two true hold-up horses are racing slightly out of their ideal role, but if the race sets up with enough early tempo to string the field and create a closing run, their finishing kick could prove decisive; It's Life's recent win and trainer's sharp 3/4 record in the last 14 days supports a live each-way interest despite the compromised position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Battle; Leader Beaten Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected rival pushes up to challenge Beryl's Girl early, forcing a contested pace that depletes both leaders.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop would see Beryl's Girl's advantage eroded, opening the door for a fresh-legged closer from the rear; West Hill Rosie is the one to note negatively here given the fade-in-finish flag, while Port Darwin's versatility gives him a chance if energy is expended up front.

watchPoints.text: Beryl's Girl's unchallenged lead is the defining tactical factor — if she jumps cleanly and gets to the front without contest, the entire complexion of the race is set and hold-up runners will need a strong finish to peg her back.

West Hill Rosie carries a recorded tendency to fade in the finish and arrives after 45 days off; if she is held up at the rear of a slowly-run race, the combination of layoff fitness and stamina fade could see her beaten well before the post.

Annexation, It's Life, and West Hill Rosie are all natural hold-up types compressed into a midfield role by the race shape — watch for traffic issues or a lack of clear daylight in the straight as three closers try to find gaps behind a single front-runner.

It's Life's trainer Kathy Turner has struck with 3 of her last 4 runners (75% strike rate in 14 days) — the form uptick and stable confidence make this one of the stronger outside angles even if the running style is somewhat out of role in this shape.

Brighton's uphill finish over 1m2f rewards horses that travel smoothly into the final turn rather than those who need to make up significant ground; any runner caught wide turning in will face extra ground and a stamina test that could expose those already running out of their natural position.

races.name: Jenningsbet "we Love Brighton Racecourse" 'confined' Handicap Stakes (For Horses Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)

runners_data.name: Redredrobin
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who handles Good ground well (1W2P from 9 similar-going runs) but has finished 9th twice recently at this trip; at 9 years old needs a truly run race to land a blow from off the pace.

runners_data.name: The Organiser
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up runner with a decent second on Good ground in his recent history; Pat Cosgrave provides a jockey upgrade but sprint finish tracks suggest the horse operates just below winning level.

runners_data.name: Havana Mojito
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose form is a striking sequence of placed efforts — six seconds across Good ground — and he is perfectly positioned by style to track King Cherry and pounce; Ashley Lewis (3) claiming is worth monitoring but the structural advantage is clear.

runners_data.name: Berning Hot
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater sends out a horse in decent form (13d T14 strike-rate context, 1 win from 15 in similar going) whose true home is at the rear of the field; forced into a midfield map position by the volume of hold-up types here, his chance is tempered by racing away from his natural tactical comfort zone.

runners_data.name: King Cherry
runners_data.note: Brighton's lone pace-setter today who won twice in 33 starts for Stuart Williams this 14-day window; no front-running rival to pressure him and Good to Firm ground suits his profile, making him the key race-shape setter.

runners_data.name: Quite Sweet
runners_data.note: Flagged as a hold-up runner who fades in the finish and has no wins on firm-side going in recent runs; displaced to midfield on the map by the sheer number of true closers in this field, her chance is further dulled by that tendency to weaken late.

runners_data.name: Viking Glory
runners_data.note: James Owen's three-year-old is a hold-up type with Good-ground placed form at 6f; stepping back to that style here after sprint experiments, though the 7f trip and Brighton's contours may catch him out if the pace is slow.

runners_data.name: Daley T
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's six-year-old operates as a true hold-up horse on Flat fast ground but has recent runs on Flat sharp tracks at shorter trips; mapped to midfield due to the hold-up congestion, his best chance is an accidentally messy race where he stumbles into a gap.

runners_data.name: Miraflores
runners_data.note: Rachel Cook and John Bridger's four-year-old has a consistent record of near-miss finishes in the 4th-9th range on Good and Standard going; a genuine rear-of-field runner slotted into midfield on the map because the hold-up cluster is too large, and the stable's 14-day window (1 from 12) suggests no particular confidence angle.

races.paceDynamic: King Cherry is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push him along, he should secure a comfortable lead at his own tempo on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's undulating 7f. The pace is therefore likely to be honest but not brutal — sustainable enough that King Cherry dictates rhythm rather than being burned up early, which compresses the finishing kick available to the hold-up brigade. The field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up types — Berning Hot, Quite Sweet, Daley T and Miraflores are all true rear-of-field horses redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there are too many hold-up runners for the race shape to accommodate them all at the back — meaning genuine prominent coverage behind King Cherry will be thin, and Havana Mojito is best placed to exploit that gap. This race shape favours a prominent racer who tracks the leader across the downhill section and hits the rising finish with energy to spare, giving the profile of Havana Mojito a structural edge that the clustered hold-up runners will struggle to match.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Cherry Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry controls the pace unchallenged and the hold-up horses fail to generate sufficient momentum from the rear
scenarios.body: King Cherry sets a measured gallop and Havana Mojito, tracking closely in second, strikes as the field climbs to the line; the large body of hold-up types are caught wide or flat-footed as the race fails to truly set them alight

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Rush Lands the Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from the outset and the race develops into a genuine test of stamina on the fast surface
scenarios.body: A true-run race stretches the field and the best hold-up runner who finds clean daylight finishes fastest; Redredrobin or Viking Glory, with genuine Good going form, could pick up the pieces if Havana Mojito overcooks the pace

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: King Cherry Leads All the Way
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so steady that King Cherry builds a commanding lead and the closers are asked for too much, too late
scenarios.body: King Cherry's hold on the race goes unbroken as hold-up runners fail to reel him in up the rise; the race simply runs too slowly to generate the bunched finish that would expose his limitations

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If the start is ragged or multiple hold-up horses push forward unexpectedly, creating a disorganised gallop
scenarios.body: Positional confusion scrambles the race shape and a horse who weaves through traffic at the right moment benefits; Daley T or Miraflores, racing out of their natural role but landing a fortunate gap, could sneak into the frame

watchPoints.text: Havana Mojito's repeated second-place finishes on Good ground make him the most structurally favoured runner if he slots directly behind King Cherry — watch whether Ashley Lewis (3) positions him promptly from the gate.
King Cherry's jockey Rob Hornby must judge whether to let him bowl along or conserve — if he dawdles early the hold-up runners behind could swarm, but if he goes too hard he sets up the closers.

The redistribution of Berning Hot, Quite Sweet, Daley T and Miraflores means the midfield will be unusually congested; watch for traffic problems approaching Brighton's final turn that could trap multiple runners simultaneously.

Viking Glory has shown placed form at 6f on Good ground but has also been well beaten at 5f — at 7f on this track the stamina question is live, and Cieren Fallon may push forward earlier than the horse's style suggests.

Quite Sweet's "fades in finish" flag is significant on a track where the final rise to the line rewards those arriving with energy; if the pace is slow her early forward movement could reverse sharply in the final furlong.

races.name: Free Race Replays On Attheraces.com Handicap Stakes (Brighton Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Pop Dancer
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old Tony Carroll runner returning after 339 days off — a significant layoff flag — but has solid course form on Good and similar going (1W3P from 15 runs), is a natural front-runner who will need to find her best quickly at this age and fresh.|

runners_data.name: Kento
runners_data.note: Consistent recent form (351233) and just 29 days since last run keeps him sharp; William Carson rides for the same Tony Carroll yard and he's posted a win and four places on similar going, though the front-running battle with stablemate Pop Dancer and Starsong complicates his chance of controlling the race.|

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's eight-year-old arrives on 21 days' rest with a win over 5f on Good in his recent history and the visor (v) headgear suggests connections want sharper concentration; naturally prominent, he could be the chief beneficiary if he gets a clean pitch just behind the contested pace.|

runners_data.name: Faustus
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse by style who handles Good going (0W3P from nine runs) and the blinkered headgear (b) focuses him; Ryan Kavanagh claims 3lb which helps, and he is best positioned of all to capitalise if the three front-runners run each other ragged, though his win-less recent record is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's seven-year-old is the freshest of the front-runners at just 10 days since last run and boasts the best similar-going record of the pace brigade (2W4P); low OR of 51 means she carries least weight but faces a fierce early battle for the lead that her stamina-biased profile may not survive.|

runners_data.name: Titus Thor
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — damaging in a race where the pace will be strong throughout; his 5f-6f form on Good shows zero wins or places across his last five, and Edward Greatrex cannot easily compensate for a horse whose form figures (70-955) speak for themselves.|

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's hold-up type brings blinkered headgear and closes from the rear; his best efforts (3/6f/GOO, 5/6f/GOO) show he can be competitive at this level on this ground, and Christian Howarth's 3lb claim is a small boost, though the lack of a course win and modest OR of 45 limit expectations.|

races.paceDynamic: Pop Dancer, Kento, and Starsong are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a strong early gallop on this flat 5½f Brighton sprint on Good to Firm ground. All three will jostle for the lead from the gates, meaning none can dictate at a controlled tempo — the pace will be pressured and relentless from the outset. Secret Handsheikh will attempt to track the leaders prominently, while Faustus and Coast will be drawn into a waiting game from the rear. With three genuine pace horses burning each other off, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race just off a fast pace or close from midfield, as the leaders are likely to tie each other up and leave the door open for a stalker or late finisher to mow them down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other off in a contested early duel, leaving them vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Pop Dancer, Kento, and Starsong set a fierce pace that exhausts each other, and the race falls to Faustus or Coast closing from the rear into a weakening field. Hold-up horses get the run of the race as the pace-setters fold, and Brighton's flat straight gives closers a clean run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Survivor From The Front
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner breaks cleanly and establishes a length advantage early, the others can't sustain pressure and drop away.
scenarios.body: The pace setter who gets the best early position conserves enough energy relative to the others to hold on as rivals collide behind, with Good to Firm ground rewarding those who travel smoothly. Pop Dancer's class on similar going and Kento's recent form make them the most likely beneficiaries if they can steal a march.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Handsheikh tracks the pace closely and pounces as the front-runners tie each other up entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Secret Handsheikh showed a win over 5f on Good and has prominent racing style that suits sitting just behind a contested pace, and the visor headgear suggests sharpened focus. Cieren Fallon can time a challenge to perfection and this horse's course-distance form gives it a tangible each-way claim.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly well-regulated and one of the front-runners finds a clear rail and dictates without serious pressure.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires two of the three front-runners to concede the lead without a fight, which contradicts all three horses' natural tendencies. Starsong's low OR of 51 and extensive similar-going experience means she would be best placed to take advantage if rivals go too wide or miss the break, but this outcome is genuinely unlikely given the confirmed pace configuration.

watchPoints.text: Watch the battle between Pop Dancer, Kento, and Starsong in the first furlong — if all three are locked together wide, none may have the energy to hold on and the entire race could play into Faustus or Coast's hands.
Pop Dancer's 339-day absence is a serious fitness concern for a nine-year-old front-runner — monitor early going reports and paddock behaviour for any sign she is not at her sharpest.

Titus Thor's flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a live concern in a race where the pace will be relentlessly strong — avoid backing him in any scenario that requires him to sustain his effort past the two-furlong pole.

Secret Handsheikh's visor headgear is newly applied or significant enough to flag — if he jumps cleanly and sits a length off the lead rather than being sucked into the pace battle, he becomes considerably more dangerous than his OR of 58 implies.

Coast and Faustus both carry blinkered headgear — two hold-up horses with the same focus equipment may track each other closely in the rear, and whichever gets the cleaner run into the straight will have a significant advantage over the other.
